allies.rationale_text: Cognitive-load-theory helps anchoring work well by using familiar schemas to reduce working-memory burden during early orientation.
allies.affinity_rationale: Explains the benefit mechanism — 'Strategic anchoring reduces cognitive load' by connecting new concepts to existing schemas — but describes what anchoring achieves rather than how CLT strengthens anchoring's effectiveness.
allies.activation_condition: When presenting new information and can connect it to existing schemas to reduce working memory burden and improve processing efficiency

allies.rationale_text: Narratives gives anchoring a memorable context that can orient attention before facts are unpacked in detail.
allies.source_quote: Stories are highly effective anchors because they lodge in memory easily and get into the brain faster than raw data or statistics.
allies.affinity_rationale: Specific amplification mechanism — 'Stories are highly effective anchors because they lodge in memory easily and get into the brain faster than raw data, often by triggering emotions' — describes how stories make anchors stick.
allies.activation_condition: When an initial reference point needs to be memorable and emotionally engaging to lodge effectively as an anchor in the audience's thinking

antagonists.rationale_text: Critical-thinking pushes back on anchoring by demanding that the first frame stay corrigible in the face of new evidence.
antagonists.source_quote: Anchoring is diametrically opposed to critical thinking, which demands questioning one's own biases and continually updating beliefs based on new data.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: The strongest adversarial language in the corpus — 'Anchoring is diametrically opposed to critical thinking, which demands questioning one's own biases and continually updating beliefs based on new data.'
antagonists.activation_condition: When the anchoring effect is driving decisions and the decision-maker needs to step back, question the reference point, and update beliefs based on the full evidence base

antagonists.rationale_text: Base-rates counters anchoring by replacing the inside-view frame with an outside-view reference point grounded in broader outcomes.
antagonists.source_quote: decision-making should be anchored instead to the outside view, focusing on general outcomes and external data
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Direct replacement mechanism — 'decision-making should be anchored instead to the outside view, focusing on general outcomes and external data' — provides the alternative reference point that displaces arbitrary anchors.
antagonists.activation_condition: When salient initial figures or anecdotes are displacing population-level frequency data from the estimate or decision

structured_tensions.tension_text: Anchoring conflicts with critical-thinking when the first frame becomes sticky enough to block real belief revision.
structured_tensions.source_quote: Anchoring is diametrically opposed to critical thinking, which demands questioning one's own biases and continually updating beliefs based on new data.

curation_notes.summary: Layer 1+2 enrichment complete. Allies: narratives 0.90 (strong — 'highly effective anchors'), cognitive-load-theory 0.80 (moderate — benefit mechanism). Antagonists: critical-thinking 0.95 (critical — 'diametrically opposed'), base-rates 0.90 (strong — direct replacement). Activation conditions assigned. SPARSE_ALLY_RECOVERY: only 2 allies.
